properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Raised 2026-08-13 while putting `req:linking-two-projects-is-a-served-process` to Anthony, flagged before he accepted it, and he accepted anyway — so the requirement stands and this stays open beneath it rather than blocking it.

HIS ASK USED "2+": *"a process that we can reuse when a user wants to link 2+ reflow2 projects"*. THE SKILL THAT SHIPPED IS PAIRWISE, and does not say so.

WHAT THE TOOLS ACTUALLY DO, checked rather than assumed:
  · `seam_report` takes a LIST of pairs, so it already composes across many boundaries in one call.
  · `pair_designs` takes exactly ONE other design. Three projects therefore means three runs (or six, if every pair is checked), and **nothing aggregates the results** — no report says "these five designs, taken together, have these seams and these unmet needs."

⇒ THE GAP IS NOT IN THE PROCESS BUT IN WHAT COLLECTS IT. Each pairwise answer is correct; there is no whole-neighbourhood view, and a user with five interrelated designs would have to hold that in their head.

📌 THIS IS WHERE `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` LIVES — ten reflow2 designs sit under `~/project`, all Anthony's, which is exactly the N-project case and the one place a shared vocabulary needs no negotiation (see the "strongest narrow form" note on `dec:idea-defined-pair-types-so-two-projects-combine-by-lookup`). And `req:many-people-and-many-projects-compose` already says the two axes must hold TOGETHER, which neither accepted requirement states.

THE OPTIONS, none taken:
A — SAY IT PLAINLY. One line in the skill's "Honest limits": it links two designs at a time, and N projects means N-1 or N(N-1)/2 runs with no aggregation. Cheapest, honest, and consistent with every other skill stating what it cannot do. **Does nothing for the user with five designs.**
B — LET THE SKILL LOOP. Prescribe running the pairwise process over each pair and collating by hand. No code, but it puts on the user exactly the bookkeeping a tool should carry, and it will be skipped.
C — A NEIGHBOURHOOD REPORT. Something that takes several designs and answers once — seams, unmet needs, dead surfaces across the set. Real work, and it needs the correspondence to be RECORDED rather than re-asserted per run, which is the same unbuilt prerequisite step 7 names.
D — NOTHING YET. Wait for a real three-project case. reflow2↔flo2 is the only pair anyone has actually linked, and building an N-way view off a sample of one is the mistake the pairing measurements already warn about.

⚠️ THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO MY OWN FLAG: I generalised "distrust the name matcher" from a single pair, and D says the same caution applies here. A neighbourhood report designed before anyone has linked three real projects would be designed from imagination.

⇒ A IS OWED REGARDLESS AND COSTS ONE LINE — a skill whose ethos is stating its own limits currently does not state this one. C is the interesting one and should wait for evidence.
properties.name: OPEN — the user asked for "2+" projects and what shipped is pairwise; should link-projects handle N, or say plainly that it handles two?
properties.rationale:
Recorded so a flag the user moved past is not lost. He asked for "2+", the shipped skill is pairwise, and the skill does not admit it — which matters more than usual because that skill's whole ethos is naming what it cannot do.

The measurement underneath it: seam_report already takes a list of pairs and composes; pair_designs takes one other design and nothing aggregates across a set. So the gap is in what COLLECTS the answers, not in the process itself.

Kept separate from dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects (where the graph lives for one owner with many projects) and from the pairing-mechanism decision, though both are adjacent — this one is narrowly about whether a shipped skill overstates its own scope.

NOTE ON THIS NODE'S OWN HISTORY: the first write of it carried a malformed tail in this field, absorbed from a broken tool call. Corrected in place the same minute; the decision text was unaffected.
